source_contract.wave_css: display block; width100%; height clamp(34px,4vw,66px); margin-bottom -1px

target_fact: All four empty Atomic divider containers render stable Elementor element classes even though stored legacy _css_classes=af-source-wave is not emitted by Elementor 4.2.4.

supersedes_for_wave_visuals.previous_direction: Attach native V4 class g-af-src-wave to all four Atomic containers.
supersedes_for_wave_visuals.reason_for_supersede: The already-existing af-source-wave CSS uses a diagonal linear-gradient approximation rather than the exact source SVG shape. Direct ID-class styling is both more exact and avoids Atomic settings mutation/D18 risk.
supersedes_for_wave_visuals.keep_previous_evidence: g-af-src-wave remains a proven V4 bridge generally, but it is no longer the preferred page256 wave fix.

css.scope: body.page-id-256 plus four elementor-element IDs only

deployment_gate: Current STATE.md scope must first be reconciled to page256.
WPVibe +5 profile/site/quota must be freshly verified.
Fresh target DOM must still contain exactly the four expected empty divider containers in the same order.
Fresh Additional CSS must contain exactly one af-project:end and no af-bio-wave-source-v001 marker.
Fresh page256 baseline must match accepted state or be reconciled before write.
postdeploy: Read back CSS marker/hash and unchanged page256 Elementor data.
Existing two-tab source/target screenshot check at all four boundaries.
Do not additionally attach g-af-src-wave unless a separate proven need exists.
Only after visual proof consider source .wave + .section reduced-top-padding mapping; do not bundle it blindly because current target section heights have existing acceptance constraints.
